source_document.body:
Container shipping spot rates from Asia to the United States declined in the latest week as offered capacity increased on routes to both U.S. coasts, according to Xeneta’s latest market update.
Average rates to the U.S. West Coast fell 1.7% to $8,203 per 40-foot container (FEU), while rates to the U.S. East Coast dropped 1.9% to $10,901 per FEU, for the week ending Nov. 19.
The declines accompanied a substantial expansion in offered capacity. Based on four-week rolling averages, capacity from the Far East to the West Coast increased 10.9% from October 19, while capacity to the East Coast rose 11.4%.
“Offered capacity is increasing on all fronthauls out of the Far East to Europe and the U.S., with average spot rates unsurprisingly continuing to soften – with one exception,” said Peter Sand, Xeneta chief analyst.
Trans-Pacific rates remain sharply above year-ago
Despite the declines, trans-Pacific spot rates remained roughly four times their year-earlier levels. Far East–U.S. West Coast rates were up 304.3% from November 19, 2025, while East Coast rates were 297.8% higher.
The figures show that the latest easing has done little to erase the substantial year-over-year increase in shipping costs on either U.S. trade lane.
Trade lane | Spot rate, November 19 | Weekly change | Year-over-year change | Monthly offered capacity change*
Far East–U.S. West Coast | $8,203/FEU | -1.7% | 304.3% | 10.9%
Far East–U.S. East Coast | $10,901/FEU | -1.9% | 297.8% | 11.4%
Far East–North Europe | $3,438/FEU | -2.3% | 44.7% | 0.2%
Far East–Mediterranean | $4,989/FEU | 6.8% | 68.7% | 2.2%
North Europe–U.S. East Coast | $2,961/FEU | Effectively unchanged | 86.8% | 38.7%
(Source: Xeneta. Offered capacity changes compare four-week rolling averages with October 19, 2026.)
On the trans-Atlantic North Europe–U.S. East Coast route, rates were effectively unchanged for the week at $2,961 per FEU, despite offered capacity rising 38.7% from a month earlier. Rates on that trade remained 86.8% above year-earlier levels.
The U.S. market averted a possible strike at the Port of Los Angeles-Long Beach this past week as employers reached a tentative contract agreement with watchmen represented by the International Longshore and Warehouse Union .
Mediterranean bucks downward trend
The main exception to falling rates on Far East export trades was the Mediterranean, where average spot rates rose 6.8% to $4,989 per FEU despite a 2.2% monthly increase in offered capacity.
That pushed the Mediterranean premium over North Europe to $1,551 per FEU. Rates to North Europe fell 2.3% during the week to $3,438.
Sand said a slowdown in container shipping’s return to the Red Sea may help explain the divergence.
Container ship transits through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at the southern end of the Red Sea increased from 305 in August to 463 in October. That recovery subsequently reversed, with the seven-day average falling 28% from a peak of 16.6 daily transits on October 25 to 11.9 on November 19.
“Something has happened to cool the return of container shipping services to the Red Sea in November,” Sand said. “Whatever the reason, disruption in the Red Sea is felt more acutely on trades between the Far East and the Mediterranean because they are the most operationally exposed to the region.”
Attacks on shipping continue to encompass a wide geographical range. Ukraine launched drone attacks on Russian ships in Libya, and vessels have been targeted off Bulgaria and Romania in the Black Sea, as well as in the Baltics.
Why It Matters: For U.S. importers, cargo owners and forwarders, expanding trans-Pacific capacity and declining weekly spot rates point to some easing in shipping costs, but rates remain roughly four times year-ago levels.
